definition: In computer vision, speeded up robust features (SURF) is a local feature detector and descriptor, with patented applications.
details: It can be used for tasks such as object recognition, image registration, classification, or 3D reconstruction. It is partly inspired by the scale-invariant feature transform (SIFT) descriptor. The standard version of SURF is several times faster than SIFT and claimed by its authors to be more robust against different image transformations than SIFT. To detect interest points, SURF uses an integer approximation of the determinant of Hessian blob detector, which can be computed with 3 integer operations using a precomputed integral image. Its feature descriptor is based on the sum of the Haar wavelet response around the point of interest. These can also be computed with the aid of the integral image. SURF descriptors have been used to locate and recognize objects, people or faces, to reconstruct 3D scenes, to track objects and to extract points of interest. SURF was first published by Herbert Bay, Tinne Tuytelaars, and Luc Van Gool, and presented at the 2006 European Conference on Computer Vision. An application of the algorithm is patented in the United States. An "upright" version of SURF (called U-SURF) is not invariant to image rotation and therefore faster to compute and better

explainer.lead: SURF is a local feature detector and descriptor used in computer vision, partly inspired by SIFT. Its value is speed: the standard version is several times faster than SIFT and claimed by its authors to be more robust across image transformations.

tiers.eli5: It finds distinctive spots in a picture, like corners and blobs, and describes them so the same spot can be matched in another picture.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use SURF for object recognition, image registration, classification and 3D reconstruction. A pitfall is that its applications are patented, which constrains where it can be deployed.
tiers.paperLevel: Detection uses an integer approximation of the determinant of the Hessian blob detector, computable with integer operations; it detects and describes local features for matching. Known limits: patented applications, and robustness/speed claims are the authors' own relative to SIFT.

explainer.example: Matching two photos of the same building for image registration by detecting SURF interest points in each and pairing the descriptors.
